notes: To add a camera, append an object to 'cameras'. The UI renders the toolbar from 'layout.groups' + 'settings' — no code changes needed. Any setting absent from 'settings' simply won't render for that camera. Discrete settings need: type, label, options[{value,label}], default. Range settings need: type, label, min, max, step, default. Optional keys: usable_max/usable_note (warning highlight), kelvin (sub-range for white_balance), beginner (tooltip text).

iso.beginner: How sensitive the sensor is to light. Higher ISO = brighter photo but more grain.

aperture.label: Aperture
aperture.beginner: The size of the lens opening. Low f-numbers (f/4) let in more light and blur the background; high f-numbers (f/16) keep more in focus.

shutter_speed.label: Shutter speed

exposure_comp.label: Exp. comp

exposure_comp.label: Exp. comp
exposure_comp.beginner: Nudges the overall brightness up (+) or down (−) without touching ISO, shutter or aperture.

white_balance.label: White balance
white_balance.beginner: Tells the camera what 'white' is under the current light, so colors look natural.

picture_style.label: Picture Control
picture_style.beginner: The camera's built-in 'look': contrast, color and sharpness recipe applied to the JPEG.

focus_mode.label: Focus mode
focus_mode.beginner: AF-S locks focus for still subjects; AF-C keeps tracking moving subjects; AF-A hands the decision to the camera.

metering_mode.label: Metering
metering_mode.beginner: Which part of the frame the camera uses to judge brightness. Spot reads a tiny area; Matrix reads the whole scene.
